text:
ash: heads up — seeing a slow, sustained drop in KV prefix hit-rate across several prod-GPU hosts starting ~2h ago after the kernel-selection heuristic rollout. per-host hit-rate down ~12-18%, p50 token latency +35-50ms. suspect eviction wave / thrash from new kernel choices.

maya: confirmed on shard-7 and shard-11. eviction count spiked around 03:25 UTC, correlates with canary -> 50% rollout. tenant-456 has a bursty batching pattern. :thinking_face:

jin: @ash did we flip the `enable_kern_v2` flag last night? I remember a tweak to prefer tiled kernels for long sequences.

ash: yes — rollout started 03:12 UTC, canary->gradual. flag: `enable_kern_v2=true`. full rollout at ~03:30.

sam: quick collect: attaching the eviction log excerpt and cache stats I pulled from one affected host:

```
2026-03-18T03:24:58Z shard=shard-7 evictions=1245 hit_rate=0.62
2026-03-18T03:26:01Z shard=shard-7 evictions=3090 hit_rate=0.48
2026-03-18T03:28:10Z shard=shard-7 evictions=4122 hit_rate=0.41
kv_prefix_entries=1.2M kv_prefix_capacity=1.6M
```

lisa: interesting — hit-rate decline is gradual but sustained, not a one-off. suggests changed access pattern + different kernel latencies lengthening request durations so eviction TTL/aging kicks in.

infra-bot: deploy event: `kernel-heuristic-v2` promoted to prod at 03:31 UTC by deployer-ci (sha: a1b2c3).

maya: i profiled KV handler on an affected host. seeing more frequent `compact_prefix()` calls and longer lock hold times. small snippet: `mutex_hold_ms median 4.1 -> 12.9` after rollout.

jin: that fits — longer handler time means KV can't serve as many gets per second, active set grows, TTL-based eviction starts pruning prefixes that are still hot. noisy tenant + batching could amplify.

ash: can we confirm a noisy neighbor? any single tenant driving 30-40% of gets? sam?

sam: yes — tenant-456 accounts for ~38% of prefix queries on shard-7 during the window. pattern: repeated short prefixes with high churn (likely streaming chat client reconnects).

lisa: mitigation suggestions: 1) rollback kernel-heuristic-v2 to restore prior latency profile 2) temporarily increase KV prefix TTL for affected shards 3) throttle tenant-456 at routing layer 4) pin kernel selection per-tenant while we analyze.

ash: i kicked off a rollback to kernel-heuristic-v1 on the canary cluster (03:47 UTC). monitoring now.

ops-bot: action taken: route-limit applied to tenant-456 (limit=200r/s) by ops at 03:50 UTC.

sam: after rollback on canary, shard-7 hit_rate recovered from 0.41 -> 0.72 within ~6m. p50 latency back down ~30ms. rolling rollback to remaining hosts now.

jin: good signal. let's avoid full config flip until we understand how v2 interacts with high-churn prefixes.

lisa: for post-mortem: collect kernel selection traces, per-request kernel decision, and KV lock hold histograms. also run synthetic replay of tenant-456 request pattern against both kernels.

ash: noted. immediate next: finish rollback, revert global flag, and schedule replay job. longer term: add heuristic to detect high-churn prefixes and prefer the faster kernel or bypass certain cache compactions.

sre-oncall: alert noise reduced, but leaving increased retention on eviction metrics for 72h. creating incident ticket INC-2026-382 for follow-up and timeline.

maya: one more datapoint — we saw a small number of `prefix_key_poison` log lines on two hosts, likely caused by an interaction between new kernel's compaction order and prefix hashing. logging those IDs for the replay.

ash: thanks — saving logs and linking to the incident. tl;dr: kernel-selection heuristics caused subtle latency increase under noisy-churn patterns, amplified KV evictions and caused slow hit-rate collapse. rollback + tenant throttle stabilized system. next: replay + targeted heuristic and TTL tuning. :thumbsup:
